column1: # edge-containers-2.tsv — MUTATION edge cases: copy-returning vs
# in-place words, the flex family, and Store/context layering.
# The mutation contract has three tiers (EXPLANATION.md "Immutability
# and mutability"; eng/go/core_storage.go):
#   * plain Map/List: set/push/pop/shift/unshift are COPY-RETURNING —
#     a new spine comes back, the receiver never changes;
#   * FlexMap/FlexList: set and the list-mutation family mutate IN
#     PLACE and return the SAME node (identity-verified here with eq);
#   * Store (context) and class instances: set mutates in place and
#     returns NOTHING — `def r (x set …)` binds nothing at all.
# Sub-engine layering: `do`/`each` children inherit the context store
# for READS, their WRITES are local and vanish; a fn body runs in the
# SAME engine, so its context writes persist. Flex nodes are shared
# pointers, so flex MUTATION inside a sub-engine does persist.
# §1  plain Map/List — copy-returning, receiver untouched
def m {a:1} def m2 (m set b 2) (m eq m2)
column3: map set returns a NEW spine — not the receiver

column1: def m {a:1} def m2 (m set a 1) (m eq m2)
column3: even a value-identical overwrite returns a fresh map

column1: def m {a:1} (m set b 2) drop m
column3: the receiver map is untouched by the discarded copy

column1: def m {} def m2 (m set a 1) def m3 (m2 set b 2) (m2 eq m3)
column3: each chained set mints another spine

column1: def m {} def m2 (m set a 1) def m3 (m2 set b 2) m3
column3: …accumulating the writes

column1: def l [1 2] def l2 (push 3 l) (l eq l2)
column3: plain push is copy-returning

column1: def l [1 2] def l2 (set 0 9 l) (l eq l2)
column3: plain list set too

column1: def l [1 2] ((pop l) drop) eq l
column3: pop returns a fresh shorter list, not the receiver

column1: def l [1 2] (pop l) drop drop l
column3: …and the receiver still has both elements

column1: unshift 9 [1 2]
column3: plain unshift returns the grown copy

column1: def l [1 2] (unshift 0 l) drop l
column3: …receiver untouched

column1: shift [1 2]
column3: plain shift returns the shrunk copy and the element

column1: def l [1 2] (shift l) drop drop l
column3: …receiver untouched

column1: # §2  Store and class-instance set return NOTHING
def r (context set 'k' 1) r
column3: Store set yields no value — the def binds nothing

column1: def P class {x:1} def p (make P {}) def r (p set x 2) r
column3: class-instance set yields no value either

column1: def s context s set 'k' 1 end context get 'k'
column3: a write through a captured store alias reaches the context

column1: context set 'x' 1 end def s context s get 'x'
column3: a store captured AFTER a write sees it

column1: def s context context set 'j' 2 end s get 'j'
column3: …but a store captured BEFORE the write does NOT — set pushes a new layer

column1: # §3  flex set/push family — in place, returning the SAME node
def f (flex {}) ((f set a 1) eq f)
column3: flex map set returns the receiver node itself

column1: def f (flex {}) (((f set a 1) set b 2) eq f)
column3: …so chains keep operating on one node

column1: def f (flex [0]) ((set 0 5 f) eq f)
column3: FlexList indexed set returns the node

column1: def f (flex [1]) ((push 2 f) eq f)
column3: push returns the node

column1: def f (flex [1]) ((append 2 f) eq f)
column3: append returns the node

column1: def f (flex [1]) ((unshift 0 f) eq f)
column3: unshift returns the node

column1: def f (flex [1 2]) (pop f drop) eq f
column3: pop returns the node (under the popped element)

column1: def f (flex {a:1}) (f eq f)
column3: sanity: a flex node is eq to itself

column1: def f (flex [1 2]) (f deq f)
column3: …and deq to itself

column1: # §4  flex mutation ordering and the two-result words
def l (flex []) push 1 l drop push 2 l drop unshift 0 l drop l
column3: push/unshift ordering: unshift prepends

column1: def l (flex [1 2 3]) pop l drop drop shift l drop drop l
column3: pop takes the tail, shift the head

column1: pop (flex [9])
column3: pop empties the node and returns the element on top

column1: shift (flex [9])
column3: shift does too, from the front

column1: def l (flex [1]) pop l drop drop push 5 l drop l
column3: a node emptied by pop grows again by push

column1: def l (flex [1 2 3]) (size l) (pop l) drop drop (size l)
column3: size tracks the in-place shrink

column1: # §5  flex aliasing — one node behind many views
def f (flex []) do [push 7 f] drop f
column3: flex mutation inside `do` PERSISTS — the node is a shared pointer (unlike context writes)

column1: def f (flex [[1]]) def g (f get 0) push 2 g drop f
column3: mutating an extracted inner node is visible through the root

column1: def f (flex {a:{b:1}}) def g f.a set b 9 g end f.a.b
column3: a nested flex member reached twice is the same node

column1: def acc (flex []) [3 1 2] each [drop (size (push 9 acc))] drop acc
column3: the flex-accumulator pattern: each-body pushes land in the shared node

column1: def acc (flex {}) [1 2] each [drop (size (set n 5 acc))] drop acc
column3: flex map accumulator: sub-engine writes to the node persist

column1: def f (flex {}) (set a [1 2] f) drop typeof f.a
column3: a plain LIST stored into a FlexMap is adopted deep-flex (the §12 adoption rule)

column1: def P class {x:1} def p (make P {}) def f (flex {q:p}) (f.q eq p)
column3: a class INSTANCE stored in flex is NOT adopted — the handle stays shared

column1: def P class {x:1} def p (make P {}) def f (flex {q:p}) set x 9 f.q end p.x
column3: …so a write through the flex view mutates the one instance

column1: # §6  non-mutating words over flex yield PLAIN results
filter [1 gt] (flex [1 2 3])
column3: filter over a FlexList returns a plain List

column1: typeof (filter [1 gt] (flex [1 2]))
column3: …nominally plain

column1: fold [add] (flex [1 2 3]) 0
column3: fold reads the flex node like a list

column1: fold [add] (flex {a:1 b:2}) 0
column3: …and a FlexMap like a map

column1: scan [add] (flex [1 2])
column3: scan over flex

column1: keys (flex {a:1})
column3: keys of a FlexMap

column1: vals (flex {a:2})
column3: vals of a FlexMap

column1: # §7  context layering — child engines read through, write locally
context set 'x' 1 end do [context get 'x']
column3: a do-child READS the parent store through the prototype chain

column1: context set 'x' 1 end do [do [context get 'x']]
column3: …transitively through two layers

column1: context set 'x' 1 end do [context set 'x' 2 end context get 'x']
column3: a child write SHADOWS inside the child (it also VANISHES when the child ends — that shape is pinned interpreter-side only, as it currently compiles to a fallback island)

column1: do [do [context set 'w' 4 end context get 'w']]
column3: nested children can still read their own writes

column1: context set 'x' 1 end each [drop (context get 'x')] [0]
column3: each bodies read the parent store too

column1: context set 'x' 1 end context set 'x' 2 end context set 'x' 3 end context get 'x'
column3: repeated sets in ONE engine layer up — latest wins

column1: context set k/q 3 end context dot k
column3: atom keys work against the store

column1: context set 'x' 5 end def g fn [[] [Integer] [context get 'x']] (g)
column3: a fn body reads the caller's context (dynamic scope)

column1: def g fn [[] [Integer] [context set 'y' 7 end context get 'y']] (g) context get 'y'
column3: a fn body runs in the SAME engine — its context write PERSISTS after the call (contrast `do`)

column1: context deq context
column3: Stores opt out of deq as well as eq — never equal, even to themselves

column1: def s1 context def s2 context (s1 deq s2)
column3: …including two captures of the same context

column1: # §8  class-instance writes are in place and visible through every view
def P class {x:1} def p (make P {}) def q p q set x 9 end p.x
column3: an alias write mutates the one instance

column1: def P class {x:1} def p (make P {}) def l [p] (l get 0) set x 9 end p.x
column3: a write through a list element mutates it too

column1: def P class {x:1} def p (make P {}) def m {q:p} m.q set x 8 end p.x
column3: …and through a map field

column1: def P class {items:(flex [])} def p (make P {}) push 1 p.items drop p.items
column3: a flex field default is one live node per instance — reads share it
